summary: A language and virtual machine built to run the same compiled code anywhere. Sun Microsystems launched it in 1995; it became the language of enterprise servers and Android apps, and passed to Oracle when Oracle bought Sun.

icon.licence: MIT (the mark itself belongs to its owner)

events.note: James Gosling, Mike Sheridan and Patrick Naughton start the project at Sun, first named Oak.

events.label: JDK 1.0
events.note: The first public Java Development Kit, promising "write once, run anywhere".

events.label: Java 2
events.note: J2SE 1.2 splits Java into editions for desktops, servers and devices.

events.label: Java 5
events.note: J2SE 5.0 adds generics to the language.

events.label: Open source
events.note: Sun releases the Java virtual machine as free software under the GPL.

events.label: Oracle
events.note: Oracle completes its purchase of Sun and takes over Java.

events.label: Java 9
events.note: Java 9 ships with a module system and deprecates the applet API.
